title: Level up your abs
summary: NH explains why abs dominate fitness culture (Hollywood, attractiveness), argues a developed core is the single most important aesthetic area because it ties upper and lower body together, and debunks bad-ab-genetics, oblique and 'abs are made in the kitchen' myths. His method: brace hard on compounds, then superset stretch-focused ab exercises daily with low intensity and moderate-high volume.
claims: The six-pack obsession has two symptoms: skinny guys who over-diet to see abs and guys who reject abs as vain to justify a year-round gut
Ask 100 young men which muscle they want and about 90% will say abs
Abs became the cultural marker of a muscular body through movies; in 300 makeup deepened the abs and Brad Pitt in Fight Club was seen as muscular with little mass
A six-pack is a marker of sexual value; women tend to prefer it, like a thick neck over a pencil neck
A well-developed core is the most important thing for aesthetics because it bridges the upper and lower body and is where the eye goes first
A poor midsection ruins an otherwise great physique, unlike peripheral muscles such as the long head of the triceps; enhanced pros' GH/insulin guts are the extreme case
Waist size is a health indicator: excess waist fat is a burden on longevity, which is why doctors check waistline
When he chased size, his love handles grew enormous; looking back at those pictures embarrasses him
Track lean gains by your waist: if bodyweight and lifts rise but your waist grows, you are mostly getting fatter, a trap for bodybuilders following powerlifting principles
A six-pack is a visual attribute, not an indicator of athleticism; strongmen and fat athletes still have strong abs under the fat
No group should skip ab training; wide-waisted lifters won't narrow their bone structure by avoiding it and will look worse
He has a 36-inch waist from bone structure; training abs made his waist look much better than when he was young
Standing side bends with a dumbbell or plate don't train the obliques; the load is moved by spine, back and hips
For obliques, use Russian twists or side leg raises hanging or on a bench, which stretch them
Squats and deadlifts grow the obliques but do not widen the waist, because the obliques sit at the front; side fat is love handles, not obliques
Uneven ('ziplock') ab insertions are genetic but no excuse not to train; trained abs look better regardless
Abs exist for a purpose: they bridge upper and lower body, protect the organs like armour and protect the lower back
A strong core including the lower back gives a strong brace that prevents injury; rounding on deadlifts often signals a weak core giving up under load
Ab shape and number are genetic but their size is not; 'small abs' are just not hypertrophied yet, same as calves or biceps
Abs are built in the gym and revealed in the kitchen; dieting only reveals what you developed
Using the six-pack as a cutting gauge ignores individual fat distribution; he has abs year-round but stores fat on glutes and legs
Abs can be trained to have more visible segments' size but the number and placement of segments are predetermined
Core strength and visible abs are different things: strongmen have strong cores without six-packs and skinny guys can have six-packs with weak cores
Bodybuilders train abs for form through function: hypertrophy requires using the muscle's function with intensity
Use both compounds and isolation for abs; don't train them like a pure isolation bodybuilder or a pure powerlifter
Perma-cutting produced a generation of 165 lb 'aesthetic bros' with no muscle; it levels up eating disorders, not abs
If you build ab muscle, a natural six-pack is easy to keep year-round without starving; he has his in winter and summer
Muscle with some fat on top looks bigger; naturals can have abs and some fat and eat what they want
Abs on a skinny guy don't count; a six-pack only looks good surrounded by muscle, since what people want is muscularity
Six-pack-in-two-weeks programs are garbage: either you starved to reveal small abs or you already had them under fat
Never build a split around abs; work them peripherally
Superset all ab exercises between other exercises; leaving abs for the end or for home means you skip them
Early on he did lots of ab isolation but also trained everything else; his abs are now much bigger with his current method
Bracing is natural and simple: take a normal breath, not a big belly breath, and squeeze the abs to wrap the spine; no ritual needed
Don't superset ab work with heavy strength sets that require bracing; superset abs with lighter, low-intensity sets later
Beginners should start small, maybe only bracing for three months, then add stretch exercises; don't rush, you won't have a six-pack in four months
Floor crunches focus on the brace not the stretch and are not the best; any core exercise emphasising the stretch is good
The best ab variation is the one you do regularly that stretches the abs; pick one or two and do them
Train abs every day with low intensity and medium-to-high volume; start with three days a week if needed. Like calves, they are used constantly and need more
All his programs include ab work every day; compounds or isolation alone won't cut it
exercises: doesn't load the obliques; spine and hips do the work
Side leg raises (hanging or on bench)
legs hooked at top, focus on the stretch, can hold a dumbbell or medicine ball
his god-tier ab exercise; unmatched stretch
focuses on brace rather than stretch; not the best
brace with a normal breath and squeeze abs
grow the obliques and core without widening the waist
